claim: MS-275 is a Class 1 histone deacetylase (HDAC) inhibitor.
source: We report herein the identification of a small molecule inhibitor of Class 1 histone deacetylases (HDACs) that significantly enhances the GLP-1R signaling.
evidence: Stated directly in the introduction section of the manuscript.

claim: MS-275 enhances GLP-1R agonism to potentiate glucose-stimulated insulin secretion in diet-induced obese (DIO) mice.
source: We here report that a small-molecule Class 1 histone deacetylase (HDAC) inhibitor Entinostat (MS-275) enhances GLP-1R agonism to potentiate glucose-stimulated insulin secretion and decrease body weight in diet-induced obese (DIO) mice.
evidence: Directly stated in the abstract with experimental support from in vivo studies.

claim: MS-275 decreases body weight in diet-induced obese (DIO) mice.
source: We here report that a small-molecule Class 1 histone deacetylase (HDAC) inhibitor Entinostat (MS-275) enhances GLP-1R agonism to potentiate glucose-stimulated insulin secretion and decrease body weight in diet-induced obese (DIO) mice.
evidence: Directly stated in the abstract with experimental support from in vivo studies.

claim: MS-275 is not an agonist or allosteric activator of GLP-1R.
source: MS-275 is not an agonist or allosteric activator of GLP-1R but enhances the sustained receptor-mediated signaling through the modulation of the expression of proteins involved in the signaling pathway.
evidence: Stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data showing MS-275 does not directly activate GLP-1R.

claim: MS-275 enhances sustained receptor-mediated signaling through modulation of expression of proteins involved in the signaling pathway.
source: MS-275 is not an agonist or allosteric activator of GLP-1R but enhances the sustained receptor-mediated signaling through the modulation of the expression of proteins involved in the signaling pathway.
evidence: Stated in the abstract and supported by RNA-seq and protein expression data.

claim: MS-275 and liraglutide combined therapy improved fasting glycemia upon short-term treatment.
source: MS-275 and liraglutide combined therapy improved fasting glycemia upon short-term treatment and a chronic administration causes a reduction of obesity in DIO mice.
evidence: Stated in the abstract and supported by in vivo experimental data.

claim: Chronic administration of MS-275 and liraglutide combined therapy causes a reduction of obesity in DIO mice.
source: MS-275 and liraglutide combined therapy improved fasting glycemia upon short-term treatment and a chronic administration causes a reduction of obesity in DIO mice.
evidence: Stated in the abstract and supported by in vivo experimental data.

claim: GLP-1R agonism has emerged as a preferred treatment for diabetes associated with obesity.
source: Given its glycemic efficacy and ability to reduce the body weight, glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor (GLP-1R) agonism has emerged as a preferred treatment for diabetes associated with obesity.
evidence: Stated in the abstract as established knowledge in the field.

claim: Not all patients achieve normal glucose control with incretin-based therapy.
source: Unfortunately, not all patients achieve normal glucose control, and even fewer show reversal of obesity (Amori et al., 2007).
evidence: Stated in the introduction with citation to published literature.

claim: Even fewer patients show reversal of obesity with incretin-based therapy.
source: Unfortunately, not all patients achieve normal glucose control, and even fewer show reversal of obesity (Amori et al., 2007).
evidence: Stated in the introduction with citation to published literature.

claim: Four Class 1 HDAC inhibitors were confirmed to enhance GLP-1R-mediated signaling.
source: From a relatively smaller compound library, four Class 1 HDAC inhibitors were confirmed to enhance GLP-1R-mediated signaling, the most prominent among them being the Class 1 HDAC-inhibitor named Entinostat (MS-275) (Suzuki et al., 1999; Saito et al., 1999).
evidence: Stated in the introduction and supported by screening data.

claim: MS-275 is the most prominent HDAC inhibitor among those that enhance GLP-1R-mediated signaling.
source: From a relatively smaller compound library, four Class 1 HDAC inhibitors were confirmed to enhance GLP-1R-mediated signaling, the most prominent among them being the Class 1 HDAC-inhibitor named Entinostat (MS-275) (Suzuki et al., 1999; Saito et al., 1999).
evidence: Stated in the introduction and supported by screening data.

claim: Liraglutide enhanced cAMP generation over basal, untreated control by 8.20 ± 2.84 fold.
source: Liraglutide (100 nM) enhanced cAMP generation over basal, untreated control by 8.20 ± 2.84 fold which was further increased to 17 ± 0.4 fold, 15.2 ± 0.6 fold, 23.5 ± 1.4 fold, and 31.7 ± 3.1 fold in presence of SAHA, TSA, AR-42, and MS-275 respectively (n = 2 replicates per treatment).
evidence: Stated in Figure 1A legend and shown in the figure.

claim: SAHA increased liraglutide-mediated cAMP generation to 17 ± 0.4 fold over basal.
source: Liraglutide (100 nM) enhanced cAMP generation over basal, untreated control by 8.20 ± 2.84 fold which was further increased to 17 ± 0.4 fold, 15.2 ± 0.6 fold, 23.5 ± 1.4 fold, and 31.7 ± 3.1 fold in presence of SAHA, TSA, AR-42, and MS-275 respectively (n = 2 replicates per treatment).
evidence: Stated in Figure 1A legend and shown in the figure.

claim: TSA increased liraglutide-mediated cAMP generation to 15.2 ± 0.6 fold over basal.
source: Liraglutide (100 nM) enhanced cAMP generation over basal, untreated control by 8.20 ± 2.84 fold which was further increased to 17 ± 0.4 fold, 15.2 ± 0.6 fold, 23.5 ± 1.4 fold, and 31.7 ± 3.1 fold in presence of SAHA, TSA, AR-42, and MS-275 respectively (n = 2 replicates per treatment).
evidence: Stated in Figure 1A legend and shown in the figure.

claim: AR-42 increased liraglutide-mediated cAMP generation to 23.5 ± 1.4 fold over basal.
source: Liraglutide (100 nM) enhanced cAMP generation over basal, untreated control by 8.20 ± 2.84 fold which was further increased to 17 ± 0.4 fold, 15.2 ± 0.6 fold, 23.5 ± 1.4 fold, and 31.7 ± 3.1 fold in presence of SAHA, TSA, AR-42, and MS-275 respectively (n = 2 replicates per treatment).
evidence: Stated in Figure 1A legend and shown in the figure.

claim: MS-275 increased liraglutide-mediated cAMP generation to 31.7 ± 3.1 fold over basal.
source: Liraglutide (100 nM) enhanced cAMP generation over basal, untreated control by 8.20 ± 2.84 fold which was further increased to 17 ± 0.4 fold, 15.2 ± 0.6 fold, 23.5 ± 1.4 fold, and 31.7 ± 3.1 fold in presence of SAHA, TSA, AR-42, and MS-275 respectively (n = 2 replicates per treatment).
evidence: Stated in Figure 1A legend and shown in the figure.

claim: MS-275 demonstrated a dose-dependent enhancement of liraglutide-mediated cAMP generation.
source: Treatment of BRIN-BD11 pancreatic beta cells with increasing concentrations of MS-275 demonstrated a dose-dependent enhancement of liraglutide-mediated cAMP generation (Figure 1B) revealing an EC50 of 4.09 μM (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Stated in the text and shown in Figure 1B.

claim: MS-275 has an EC50 of 4.09 μM for enhancement of liraglutide-mediated cAMP generation.
source: Treatment of BRIN-BD11 pancreatic beta cells with increasing concentrations of MS-275 demonstrated a dose-dependent enhancement of liraglutide-mediated cAMP generation (Figure 1B) revealing an EC50 of 4.09 μM (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Stated in the text and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: MS-275 treatment resulted in a 3.464 ± 0.244 fold enhancement of liraglutide-mediated cAMP generation.
source: Overall, we observed a 3.464 ± 0.244 fold enhancement of liraglutide-mediated cAMP generation upon MS-275 treatment.
evidence: Stated in the results section with experimental data.

claim: The GLP-1R antagonist Jant 4 repressed MS-275-mediated GLP-1R response.
source: The GLP-1R antagonist Jant 4 repressed this GLP-1R-mediated response highlighting the specificity of the induction (Figure 1C).
evidence: Stated in the text and shown in Figure 1C.

claim: MS-275 enhanced the agonism of IUB68, a specific GIPR ligand, in BRIN-BD11 pancreatic beta cells.
source: In a similar fashion to GLP-1R, MS-275 enhanced the agonism of IUB68, a specific glucose-dependent insulinotropic peptide receptor (GIPR) ligand in BRIN-BD11 pancreatic beta cells (Figure 1D).
evidence: Stated in the text and shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The combination of MS-275 with IUB68 was superior to either agent when tested separately.
source: The combination of the MS-275 with IUB68 was superior to either agent when tested separately.
evidence: Stated in the results section with experimental data.

claim: Liraglutide causes substantial localization of the activated GLP-1R as cytoplasmic dots even after 90 min post-internalization.
source: Our present study of GLP-1R trafficking following the activation with liraglutide revealed distinct receptor-trafficking kinetics as we observed a substantial localization of the activated receptor as cytoplasmic dots even after 90 min post-internalization (Figure 1E).
evidence: Stated in the text and shown in Figure 1E.

claim: MS-275 treatment enhanced cAMP generation at 30 min and 90 min following liraglutide treatment.
source: As Figure 1F shows, MS-275 treatment enhanced cAMP generation at 30 min and 90 min following liraglutide treatment (p<0.05 two-way ANOVA, Bonferroni post-tests) over control cells when the activated receptor had achieved substantial residence in the cytoplasm as punctate dots (Figure 1E, white arrows).
evidence: Stated in the text and shown in Figure 1F.

claim: Bafilomycin A1 is a specific inhibitor of v-ATPase that prevents late-stage vesicle maturation by suppressing endosomal acidification.
source: To validate our observation, we treated the cells with Bafilomycin A1, a specific inhibitor of v-ATPase that prevents late-stage vesicle maturation by suppressing endosomal acidification (Bayer et al., 1998).
evidence: Stated in the text with citation to published literature.

claim: Bafilomycin A1 treatment increased GLP-1R-mediated cAMP generation in control cells.
source: In control cells, we observed an increase in GLP-1R-mediated cAMP generation over basal values upon Bafilomycin A1 treatment.
evidence: Stated in the text with experimental data.

claim: In MS-275-treated pancreatic beta cells, Bafilomycin inhibition enhanced GLP-1R-mediated cAMP generation from 46.68 ± 0.95 fold to 57.7 ± 2.84 fold.
source: However, in MS-275-treated pancreatic beta cells, Bafilomycin inhibition further enhanced GLP-1R-mediated cAMP generation from 46.68 ± 0.95 fold to 57.7 ± 2.84 fold (p<0.001, n = 3; one way ANOVA Tukey's multiple comparison test), relative to the basal cAMP generation (Figure 1G).
evidence: Stated in the text and shown in Figure 1G.

claim: Inhibition of endosomal maturation enhanced MS-275-mediated GLP-1R response.
source: The data thus indicated that the inhibition of endosomal maturation enhanced MS-275-mediated GLP-1R response.
evidence: Stated as interpretation of experimental data.

claim: Inhibition of GLP-1R internalization upon expression of Rab5A S34N dominant-negative plasmid significantly reduced MS-275-mediated augmentation of GLP-1R signaling.
source: In contrast, the inhibition of GLP-1R internalization upon expression of Rab5A S34N dominant-negative plasmid (Girada et al., 2017) significantly reduced the MS-275-mediated augmentation of GLP-1R signaling (EC50129.6 nM in Rab5A S34N transfected cells as compared to EC5010.39 nM) upon control plasmid transfection (Figure 1H).
evidence: Stated in the text and shown in Figure 1H.

claim: MS-275 augments sustained cAMP generation post-activation and internalization of the receptor.
source: These results, taken together, indicated the efficacy of MS-275 to augment the sustained cAMP generation post-activation and internalization of the receptor thereby promoting prolonged GLP-1R action in the pancreatic beta cells.
evidence: Stated as interpretation of experimental data.

claim: 1858 genes were upregulated upon MS-275 treatment in BRIN-BD11 pancreatic beta cells.
source: We found that 1858 genes were upregulated and 624 genes downregulated upon MS-275 treatment (log fold change ≥±2, p-value<0.05).
evidence: Stated in the results section based on RNA-seq data.

claim: 624 genes were downregulated upon MS-275 treatment in BRIN-BD11 pancreatic beta cells.
source: We found that 1858 genes were upregulated and 624 genes downregulated upon MS-275 treatment (log fold change ≥±2, p-value<0.05).
evidence: Stated in the results section based on RNA-seq data.

claim: Upregulated pathways upon MS-275 treatment include endocytosis, cAMP signaling, insulin secretion, and PI3K-Akt signaling.
source: Gene ontology analysis of the upregulated pathways included endocytosis, cAMP signaling, insulin secretion, and the PI3K-Akt signaling, whereas the downregulated genes include histone modification, chromosome organization, and cell cycle regulation (Figure 2B).
evidence: Stated in the text and shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Downregulated pathways upon MS-275 treatment include histone modification, chromosome organization, and cell cycle regulation.
source: Gene ontology analysis of the upregulated pathways included endocytosis, cAMP signaling, insulin secretion, and the PI3K-Akt signaling, whereas the downregulated genes include histone modification, chromosome organization, and cell cycle regulation (Figure 2B).
evidence: Stated in the text and shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The cAMP signaling pathway was significantly upregulated upon MS-275 treatment (FDR < 0.25).
source: Gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) (classical scoring with 1000 permutations) revealed the cAMP signaling pathway to be significantly upregulated (FDR < 0.25) (Figure 2C).
evidence: Stated in the text and shown in Figure 2C.

claim: MS-275 treatment increased H3K27 acetylation.
source: The modulation of the transcriptome profile was reflected in the reversible chromatin alteration upon MS-275 treatment as has been manifested in increased H3K27 acetylation (Figure 2F) and in the alteration of the expression of the genes involved in global transcriptional regulation (Figure 2G) that has a significant influence on the GLP-1R signaling.
evidence: Stated in the text and shown in Figure 2F.

claim: MS-275 treatment significantly upregulated Gαs protein expression (2.44 ± 0.45 fold; n = 3) in cultured pancreatic beta cells.
source: As Figure 3A shows, MS-275 treatment significantly upregulated Gαs protein expression (2.44 ± 0.45 fold; n = 3) in cultured pancreatic beta cells.
evidence: Stated in the text and shown in Figure 3A.

claim: MS-275 treatment upregulated Gnas gene expression (log2 fold 3.54; p adjusted 0.00003).
source: The data aligned with the RNA seq data which showed the upregulation of Gnas gene expression (log2 fold 3.54; p adjusted 0.00003).
evidence: Stated in the text based on RNA-seq data.

claim: MS-275 treatment increased GLP-1R expression.
source: We observed a significant increase in GLP-1R (Figure 3B and C) and beta-arrestin−1 expression as well (Figure 3D, Figure 3F) upon MS-275 treatment that participates in the process of sustained GPCR signaling from endosomes.
evidence: Stated in the text and shown in Figures 3B and 3C.

claim: MS-275 treatment increased beta-arrestin-1 expression.
source: We observed a significant increase in GLP-1R (Figure 3B and C) and beta-arrestin−1 expression as well (Figure 3D, Figure 3F) upon MS-275 treatment that participates in the process of sustained GPCR signaling from endosomes.
evidence: Stated in the text and shown in Figures 3D and 3F.

claim: MS-275 treatment increased Adcy8 expression by 2.59 ± 0.33 fold.
source: As our data revealed, MS-275 treatment increased the Adcy8 expression by 2.59 ± 0.33 fold thereby defining the mechanism by which MS-275 enhanced the GLP-1R-mediated cAMP generation.
evidence: Stated in the text with experimental data.

claim: CCCP treatment completely abolished GLP-1R agonism in control cells.
source: CCCP treatment completely abolished the GLP-1R agonism in control cells; in contrast, significant GLP-1R-mediated cAMP generation was retained in MS-275-treated pancreatic beta cells despite CCCP dosage (Figure 3H).
evidence: Stated in the text and shown in Figure 3H.

claim: Significant GLP-1R-mediated cAMP generation was retained in MS-275-treated pancreatic beta cells despite CCCP dosage.
source: CCCP treatment completely abolished the GLP-1R agonism in control cells; in contrast, significant GLP-1R-mediated cAMP generation was retained in MS-275-treated pancreatic beta cells despite CCCP dosage (Figure 3H).
evidence: Stated in the text and shown in Figure 3H.

claim: MS-275 treatment enhanced glycolysis and maximal glycolytic activity in BRIN-BD11 pancreatic beta cells.
source: To explore it further, we carried out real-time respirometry that recorded a significant increase of glycolysis and maximal glycolytic activity upon MS-275 treatment (Figure 3I and I (i), 3I (ii)).
evidence: Stated in the text and shown in Figure 3I.

claim: MS-275 treatment upregulated GLUT2 mRNA expression.
source: We also observed a significant upregulation of GLUT2 mRNA expression upon MS-275 treatment (Figure 3K) and a corresponding increase in the basal glucose uptake (Figure 3L) that may account for the enhanced glycolysis to support the sustained cAMP generation in MS-275-treated cultured pancreatic beta cells.
evidence: Stated in the text and shown in Figure 3K.

claim: MS-275 treatment increased basal glucose uptake in BRIN-BD11 pancreatic beta cells.
source: We also observed a significant upregulation of GLUT2 mRNA expression upon MS-275 treatment (Figure 3K) and a corresponding increase in the basal glucose uptake (Figure 3L) that may account for the enhanced glycolysis to support the sustained cAMP generation in MS-275-treated cultured pancreatic beta cells.
evidence: Stated in the text and shown in Figure 3L.

claim: MS-275 treatment amplified GLP-1R-mediated insulin secretion in cultured pancreatic beta cells.
source: As Figure 4B revealed, MS-275 treatment amplified the GLP-1R-mediated insulin secretion in cultured pancreatic beta cells.
evidence: Stated in the text and shown in Figure 4B.

claim: MS-275 treatment increased GLP-1R-mediated insulin exocytosis in rat islets.
source: Similarly, in rat islets, we observed a significant increase of GLP-1R-mediated insulin exocytosis (Figure 4C).
evidence: Stated in the text and shown in Figure 4C.

claim: MS-275-mediated augmentation of GLP-1R-induced GSIS was completely abrogated upon expression of Rab 5A S34N plasmid.
source: MS-275-mediated augmentation of GLP-1R-induced GSIS was completely abrogated upon the expression of the Rab 5A S34N plasmid (Figure 4D) that reduced GLP-1R response (Figure 1H) and has earlier been reported to hinder GLP-1R internalization upon activation (Girada et al., 2017).
evidence: Stated in the text and shown in Figure 4D.

claim: MS-275-treated cultured pancreatic beta cells exposed to Bafilomycin A1 significantly stimulated liraglutide-induced GSIS.
source: Conversely, MS-275-treated cultured pancreatic beta cells, upon the exposure to Bafilomycin A1 significantly stimulated liraglutide-induced GSIS (Figure 4E).
evidence: Stated in the text and shown in Figure 4E.

claim: MS-275 treatment upregulated Synaptotagmin-8 (Syt-8) expression.
source: In agreement with the analysis, we observed MS-275-mediated upregulation of Synaptotagmin-8 (Syt-8) (Figure 4G), the t-SNARE SNAP25 (Figure 4H) as well as Anoctamin 1 (Ano 1) (Figure 4I), that regulate GSIS. (Xu et al., 2012; Al-Daghri, 2016; Crutzen et al., 2016)
evidence: Stated in the text and shown in Figure 4G.

claim: MS-275 treatment upregulated SNAP25 expression.
source: In agreement with the analysis, we observed MS-275-mediated upregulation of Synaptotagmin-8 (Syt-8) (Figure 4G), the t-SNARE SNAP25 (Figure 4H) as well as Anoctamin 1 (Ano 1) (Figure 4I), that regulate GSIS. (Xu et al., 2012; Al-Daghri, 2016; Crutzen et al., 2016)
evidence: Stated in the text and shown in Figure 4H.

claim: MS-275 treatment upregulated Anoctamin 1 (Ano 1) expression.
source: In agreement with the analysis, we observed MS-275-mediated upregulation of Synaptotagmin-8 (Syt-8) (Figure 4G), the t-SNARE SNAP25 (Figure 4H) as well as Anoctamin 1 (Ano 1) (Figure 4I), that regulate GSIS. (Xu et al., 2012; Al-Daghri, 2016; Crutzen et al., 2016)
evidence: Stated in the text and shown in Figure 4I.

claim: MS-275 treatment did not alter the expression of Synaptotagmin-7 (Syt-7).
source: Though Syt-8 and SNAP 25 expression were upregulated, we did not observe any alteration in the expression of Synaptotagmin-7 (Syt-7) (Figure 4J), which is a PKA substrate and has been reported to contribute to the GLP-1R-induced GSIS (Wu et al., 2015).
evidence: Stated in the text and shown in Figure 4J.

claim: MS-275 treatment prevented palmitate-induced death of cultured BRIN-BD11 pancreatic beta cells in a dose-dependent manner.
source: We observed palmitate-induced death of cultured BRIN-BD11 pancreatic beta cells in a dose-dependent manner, which was prevented upon MS-275 treatment. (Figure 5A).
evidence: Stated in the text and shown in Figure 5A.

claim: MS-275 treatment upregulated key enzymes of the β-oxidation pathway including Cpt1A, ACADL, ACADM, ACADS, HADH, and ACAA2.
source: GSEA analysis revealed significant upregulation of the key enzymes of the β-oxidation pathway like Cpt1A, ACADL, ACADM, ACADS, HADH, and ACAA2 when cultured pancreatic beta cells were treated with MS-275 (Figure 5B, Figure 5C).
evidence: Stated in the text and shown in Figures 5B and 5C.

claim: MS-275 treatment upregulated redox enzymes like Prdx4, Prdx1, Prdx6, Gpx2, Txnrd1, and Txnrd3 in pancreatic beta cells.
source: However, higher expression of the redox enzymes like Prdx4, Prdx1, Prdx6 as well as Gpx2, Txnrd1, and Txnrd3 in the cytoplasm of the pancreatic beta cells was observed upon MS-275 treatment (Figure 5F), which is indicative of the increased neutralization of the reactive oxidants as explained in Figure 5H.
evidence: Stated in the text and shown in Figure 5F.

claim: MS-275 treatment decreased ROS generation in pancreatic beta cells upon palmitate exposure.
source: In agreement with our RNA seq data, we observed decreased ROS generation in MS-275-treated cells upon palmitate exposure (Figure 5G) that may account for the reduced pancreatic beta cell death.
evidence: Stated in the text and shown in Figure 5G.

claim: MS-275 treatment increased maximal respiration in 3T3L1 adipocytes.
source: As the data shows, liraglutide exerted no effect on oxygen consumption rate (OCR) both in control and MS-275-treated cultured adipocytes when palmitate was used as substrate. We observed increased maximal respiration (Figure 6A (ii)) as well as ATP-linked respiration (Figure 6A (iii)) and the OCR linked to proton leak (Figure 6A (iv)) in MS-275-treated adipocytes.
evidence: Stated in the text and shown in Figure 6A(ii).

claim: MS-275 treatment increased ATP-linked respiration in 3T3L1 adipocytes.
source: As the data shows, liraglutide exerted no effect on oxygen consumption rate (OCR) both in control and MS-275-treated cultured adipocytes when palmitate was used as substrate. We observed increased maximal respiration (Figure 6A (ii)) as well as ATP-linked respiration (Figure 6A (iii)) and the OCR linked to proton leak (Figure 6A (iv)) in MS-275-treated adipocytes.
evidence: Stated in the text and shown in Figure 6A(iii).

claim: MS-275 treatment increased OCR linked to proton leak in 3T3L1 adipocytes.
source: As the data shows, liraglutide exerted no effect on oxygen consumption rate (OCR) both in control and MS-275-treated cultured adipocytes when palmitate was used as substrate. We observed increased maximal respiration (Figure 6A (ii)) as well as ATP-linked respiration (Figure 6A (iii)) and the OCR linked to proton leak (Figure 6A (iv)) in MS-275-treated adipocytes.
evidence: Stated in the text and shown in Figure 6A(iv).

claim: Liraglutide exerted no effect on oxygen consumption rate in control and MS-275-treated cultured adipocytes when palmitate was used as substrate.
source: As the data shows, liraglutide exerted no effect on oxygen consumption rate (OCR) both in control and MS-275-treated cultured adipocytes when palmitate was used as substrate.
evidence: Stated in the text with experimental data.

claim: Replacement of palmitate with fat-free BSA diminished MS-275-mediated proton leak.
source: Replacement of palmitate with the fat-free BSA diminished MS-275-mediated proton leak, which highlighted the contribution of the beta-oxidation pathway in promoting energy expenditure through proton leak in MS-275-treated cultured adipocytes.
evidence: Stated in the text with experimental data.

claim: Combined treatment of liraglutide and MS-275 reduced fasting blood glucose to 91.33 ± 3.49 mg/dL from 150.2 ± 3.53 mg/dL in control group (p<0.001).
source: As Figure 7A revealed, the fasting blood sugar level in the control group is 150.2 ± 3.53 mg/dL, whereas upon the combined treatment of liraglutide and MS-275, the blood glucose is reduced to 91.33 ± 3.49 mg/dL (p<0.001, one way ANOVA, Tukey's multiple comparison test).
evidence: Stated in the text and shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Combined therapy of MS-275 and liraglutide showed superior blood glucose reduction compared to liraglutide monotherapy (p<0.05).
source: Although both monotherapy and combined therapy revealed a significant decrease in the blood glucose, mice receiving the combined therapy displayed a superior blood glucose reduction as compared to liraglutide monotherapy (p<0.05, one–way ANOVA Tukey's multiple comparison test) or MS-275 monotherapy (p<0.01, one–way ANOVA Tukey's multiple comparison test) (Figure 7A).
evidence: Stated in the text and shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Combined therapy of MS-275 and liraglutide showed superior blood glucose reduction compared to MS-275 monotherapy (p<0.01).
source: Although both monotherapy and combined therapy revealed a significant decrease in the blood glucose, mice receiving the combined therapy displayed a superior blood glucose reduction as compared to liraglutide monotherapy (p<0.05, one–way ANOVA Tukey's multiple comparison test) or MS-275 monotherapy (p<0.01, one–way ANOVA Tukey's multiple comparison test) (Figure 7A).
evidence: Stated in the text and shown in Figure 7A.

claim: HFD feeding significantly reduced insulin content in pancreatic tissue compared to chow diet.
source: As Figure 7E shows, HFD feeding significantly reduced the insulin content as compared to the group on the chow diet, which is restored upon treatment with liraglutide or MS-275 monotherapy as well as liraglutide and MS-275 combined therapy.
evidence: Stated in the text and shown in Figure 7E.

claim: Treatment with liraglutide or MS-275 monotherapy restored insulin content reduced by HFD feeding.
source: As Figure 7E shows, HFD feeding significantly reduced the insulin content as compared to the group on the chow diet, which is restored upon treatment with liraglutide or MS-275 monotherapy as well as liraglutide and MS-275 combined therapy.
evidence: Stated in the text and shown in Figure 7E.

claim: Liraglutide and MS-275 combined therapy restored insulin content reduced by HFD feeding.
source: As Figure 7E shows, HFD feeding significantly reduced the insulin content as compared to the group on the chow diet, which is restored upon treatment with liraglutide or MS-275 monotherapy as well as liraglutide and MS-275 combined therapy.
evidence: Stated in the text and shown in Figure 7E.

claim: MS-275 and liraglutide combined treatment enhanced expression of GLP-1R and Gαs in vivo.
source: In coordination with the increase in the insulin content, MS-275 and liraglutide combined treatment enhanced the expression of the key proteins involved in the GLP-1R signaling pathway in vivo. As our data showed, the increase of GLP-1R and Gαs was the highest in mice treated with liraglutide and MS-275 combined therapy (Figure 7F and Figure 7G).
evidence: Stated in the text and shown in Figures 7F and 7G.

claim: There was a significant reduction of cumulative food intake in mice receiving combined therapy of liraglutide and MS-275 (p<0.05).
source: As Figure 8A (i) shows, there is a significant reduction of the cumulative food intake in the mice receiving combined therapy of liraglutide and MS-275 (p<0.05 one-way ANOVA, Tukey's multiple comparison test).
evidence: Stated in the text and shown in Figure 8A(i).

claim: Mice receiving dual therapy of liraglutide and MS-275 showed significant reduction in body weight gain (p<0.001).
source: The decrease in the food intake contributes to a negative energy balance resulting in a significant weight loss as we observed a reduction of the body weight gain in mice receiving the dual therapy of liraglutide and MS-275 (Figure 8A (ii), p<0.001 two way ANOVA Bonferroni post-tests).
evidence: Stated in the text and shown in Figure 8A(ii).

claim: Combined treatment of MS-275 and liraglutide significantly decreased body weight in DIO mice (p<0.001).
source: Control mice and the groups receiving liraglutide or MS-275 monotherapy showed increased body weight gain. However, in the combined treatment group there was a significant decrease in body weight (Figure 8B ii), (p<0.001, one-way ANOVA, Tukey's multiple comparison test).
evidence: Stated in the text and shown in Figure 8B(ii).

claim: After treatment holiday, mice that received combined therapy had enhanced body weight gain relative to monotherapy groups.
source: In this period, the mice that received combined therapy had enhanced body weight gain relative to their comparators that received liraglutide or MS-275 monotherapy (Figure 8B (iii)).
evidence: Stated in the text and shown in Figure 8B(iii).

claim: After treatment restoration, only the group receiving MS-275 and liraglutide combined therapy significantly reduced body weight (p<0.001).
source: We measured the weight gain every week and as the data shows, only the group receiving MS-275 and liraglutide combined therapy significantly reduced the body weight (p<0.001 two-way ANOVA Bonferroni post-tests).
evidence: Stated in the text and shown in Figure 8B(iv).

claim: MS-275 and liraglutide combined therapy reduced epididymal WAT by 34.6 ± 0.09% compared to vehicle control (p<0.001).
source: Our data showed a significant reduction of the epididymal WAT upon MS-275 and liraglutide combined therapy as compared to the vehicle control (34.6 ± 0.09%; p<0.001, one-way ANOVA, Tukey's multiple comparison test) (Figure 9A (i)).
evidence: Stated in the text and shown in Figure 9A(i).

claim: MS-275 and liraglutide combined therapy reduced mesenteric WAT to 10.36 ± 0.05% compared to vehicle control (p<0.001).
source: The mesenteric WAT in mice upon liraglutide and MS-275 combined therapy was reduced to 10.36 ± 0.05% as compared to the group receiving normal saline as vehicle control (p<0.001, one-way ANOVA, Tukey's multiple comparison test) (Figure 9A (ii)).
evidence: Stated in the text and shown in Figure 9A(ii).

claim: Combined therapy with liraglutide and MS-275 reduced retroperitoneal WAT to 32.97 ± 0.09% compared to vehicle control (p<0.01).
source: In contrast, we observed no reduction of retroperitoneal WAT mass upon liraglutide monotherapy, whereas upon combined therapy with liraglutide and MS-275 there was a reduction to 32.97 ± 0.09% as compared to the control group receiving normal saline as vehicle control (p<0.01, one-way ANOVA Tukey's multiple comparison test).
evidence: Stated in the text and shown in Figure 9A(iii).

claim: MS-275 and liraglutide combined treatment significantly increased UCP1 expression in retroperitoneal WAT compared to vehicle control.
source: However, we observed a significant increase of PGC1 alpha (Figure 9B (iii)) and UCP1 (Fig 9B (iv)) in retroperitoneal WAT upon MS-275 and liraglutide combined treatment as compared to the vehicle control that exceeds either of the two monotherapies.
evidence: Stated in the text and shown in Figure 9B(iv).

claim: MS-275 and liraglutide combined treatment significantly increased PGC1 alpha expression in retroperitoneal WAT compared to vehicle control.
source: However, we observed a significant increase of PGC1 alpha (Figure 9B (iii)) and UCP1 (Fig 9B (iv)) in retroperitoneal WAT upon MS-275 and liraglutide combined treatment as compared to the vehicle control that exceeds either of the two monotherapies.
evidence: Stated in the text and shown in Figure 9B(iii).

claim: MS-275 inhibits HDAC1 and HDAC3 with comparable potency.
source: The most effective molecule in our screening was MS-275 (also known as entinostat), a Class 1 HDAC inhibitor that inhibits HDAC1 and HDAC3 with comparable potency (Lauffer et al., 2013).
evidence: Stated in the text with citation to published literature.

claim: Increased beta-oxidation flux and generated reactive oxidants drive energy expenditure upon fatty acid oxidation in MS-275-treated cultured adipocytes.
source: The data propose that increased beta-oxidation flux and the generated reactive oxidants drives the energy expenditure upon fatty acid oxidation in MS-275-treated cultured adipocytes.
evidence: Stated as interpretation of experimental data.

claim: The 'oxidant quenching cycle' drives the proton leak and consequent futile cycle causing energy dissipation.
source: 'The oxidant quenching cycle' which is initiated with the generation of the superoxides, a by-product of the beta-oxidation pathway, and throttled by the quenching of the superoxides through the enhanced expression and activation of the antioxidant enzymes upon MS-275 treatment, drives the proton leak and the consequent futile cycle causes energy dissipation (Figure 10).
evidence: Stated as interpretation of experimental data and illustrated in Figure 10.

claim: MS-275 has been reported to cause hyperglycemia and hypertriglyceridemia as dose-limiting toxicities in some patients with refractory and relapsed acute leukemia.
source: MS-275 monotherapy can provide metabolic benefits in rodents (Galmozzi et al., 2013; Ferrari et al., 2017) but has been reported to cause hyperglycemia and hypertriglyceridemia as the dose-limiting toxicities in a few patients suffering from refractory and relapsed acute leukemia (Gojo et al., 2007).
evidence: Stated in the discussion with citation to published literature.

claim: Combined therapy of MS-275 and liraglutide showed no change in liver weight.
source: In the case of combined therapy of MS-275 and liraglutide, we observed no change in liver weight (Figure 9—figure supplement 1), and there was no fatty liver phenotype in any of the animals receiving liraglutide and MS-275 combined therapy.
evidence: Stated in the text and shown in Figure 9—figure supplement 1.

claim: There was no fatty liver phenotype in animals receiving liraglutide and MS-275 combined therapy.
source: In the case of combined therapy of MS-275 and liraglutide, we observed no change in liver weight (Figure 9—figure supplement 1), and there was no fatty liver phenotype in any of the animals receiving liraglutide and MS-275 combined therapy.
evidence: Stated in the text based on experimental observations.

claim: Combined treatment group showed a 3.13 ± 0.15 fold increase of hepatic IGF-1 (p<0.01).
source: In the combined treatment group, we observed a 3.13 ± 0.15 fold increase of hepatic IGF-1 (p<0.01, one-way ANOVA, Tukey's multiple comparison test, Figure 9—figure supplement 2) in the liver tissue that was known to have the anti-inflammatory effect (Hribal et al., 2013).
evidence: Stated in the text and shown in Figure 9—figure supplement 2.

claim: Type 2 diabetes (T2D) and obesity have reached global epidemic levels.
source: Type 2 diabetes (T2D) and obesity have reached global epidemic levels and required a therapeutic intervention to reduce the burden of the disease.
evidence: Stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claim: Incretin-based therapy provides sizable glycemic benefit and modest improvement in body weight.
source: Incretin-based therapy and specifically glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor (GLP-1R) agonists provide sizable glycemic benefit and modest improvement in the body weight (Astrup et al., 2009).
evidence: Stated in the introduction with citation to published literature.

claim: Incretin receptors can be activated by orthosteric peptide-based agonists.
source: Incretin receptors can be activated by orthosteric peptide-based agonists (Drucker et al., 2010), dual agonists (Finan et al., 2013), and small-molecule allosteric modulators (Knudsen et al., 2007; Bueno et al., 2016).
evidence: Stated in the introduction with citations to published literature.

claim: Incretin receptors can be activated by dual agonists.
source: Incretin receptors can be activated by orthosteric peptide-based agonists (Drucker et al., 2010), dual agonists (Finan et al., 2013), and small-molecule allosteric modulators (Knudsen et al., 2007; Bueno et al., 2016).
evidence: Stated in the introduction with citations to published literature.

claim: Incretin receptors can be activated by small-molecule allosteric modulators.
source: Incretin receptors can be activated by orthosteric peptide-based agonists (Drucker et al., 2010), dual agonists (Finan et al., 2013), and small-molecule allosteric modulators (Knudsen et al., 2007; Bueno et al., 2016).
evidence: Stated in the introduction with citations to published literature.

claim: Activation of GLP-1R propels a cellular signaling cascade that potentiates glucose-stimulated insulin secretion (GSIS).
source: The activation of the receptor propels a cellular signaling cascade that eventually potentiates glucose-stimulated insulin secretion (GSIS) (Drucker, 2006).
evidence: Stated in the introduction with citation to published literature.

claim: Sustained cAMP generation occurs for several GPCRs following internalization and formation of multi-protein complex at endosomes.
source: More recent reports, however, demonstrate sustained cAMP generation for several GPCRs following internalization and the formation of a multi-protein complex at endosomes where activated receptor-ligand complex, the Gαs subunit of the heterotrimeric G-protein and beta arrestin-1 contribute as key components (Thomsen et al., 2016).
evidence: Stated in the introduction with citation to published literature.

claim: Prolonged association of Gαs subunit with activated and internalized GLP-1R at Rab5 endosomes sustains cAMP generation to support GSIS in pancreatic beta cells.
source: Previous observations from our laboratory have shown that prolonged association of the Gαs subunit with the activated and internalized GLP-1R at Rab5 endosomes sustains cAMP generation to support GSIS in pancreatic beta cells (Girada et al., 2017).
evidence: Stated in the introduction with citation to previous work from the same laboratory.

claim: MS-275 is also known as entinostat.
source: The most effective molecule in our screening was MS-275 (also known as entinostat), a Class 1 HDAC inhibitor that inhibits HDAC1 and HDAC3 with comparable potency (Lauffer et al., 2013).
evidence: Stated in the introduction.

claim: SAHA, Trichostatin A, AR-42, and MS-275 are HDAC inhibitors possessing either a hydroxamate or an orthoanilide group.
source: Interestingly, each of these compounds is an HDAC inhibitor possessing either a hydroxamate or an orthoanilide group.
evidence: Stated in the results section describing the screening hits.

claim: The identified HDAC inhibitors are not direct GLP-1R agonists.
source: These compounds are not direct GLP-1R agonists as assessed by their independent inability to promote cAMP generation acutely in BRIN-BD11 pancreatic beta cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Stated in the text and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: MS-275 treatment decreased DNMT-1 gene expression (log 2 fold −0.82 p adjusted: 5.38E-17).
source: The RNA seq data presented in this study revealed a decrease in the expression of DNMT-1 gene expression upon MS-275 treatment (log 2 fold −0.82 p adjusted: 5.38E-17; Figure 2G and H) that aligned with the reduction in the relative presence of methyl cytosine as observed in the case of the calcium-sensing receptor (CaSr) promoter (Alaminos et al., 2004).
evidence: Stated in the text and shown in Figures 2G and 2H.

claim: Adcy-8 is essential for GLP-1R signaling.
source: The isoform Adcy-8, essential for GLP-1R signaling (Roger et al., 2011) was enhanced upon MS-275 treatment (Figure 3G).
evidence: Stated in the text with citation to published literature.

claim: Various subtypes of adenylyl cyclase (Adcy1-8) generate cAMP response upon GPCR activation in pancreatic beta cells.
source: Various subtypes of adenylyl cyclase (Adcy1-8) that generate cAMP response upon GPCR activation have been reported in pancreatic beta cells (Leech et al., 1999; Roger et al., 2011; Kitaguchi et al., 2013).
evidence: Stated in the text with citations to published literature.

claim: Synaptotagmin-8, SNAP25, and Anoctamin 1 regulate GSIS.
source: In agreement with the analysis, we observed MS-275-mediated upregulation of Synaptotagmin-8 (Syt-8) (Figure 4G), the t-SNARE SNAP25 (Figure 4H) as well as Anoctamin 1 (Ano 1) (Figure 4I), that regulate GSIS. (Xu et al., 2012; Al-Daghri, 2016; Crutzen et al., 2016)
evidence: Stated in the text with citations to published literature.

claim: Synaptotagmin-7 is a PKA substrate that contributes to GLP-1R-induced GSIS.
source: Though Syt-8 and SNAP 25 expression were upregulated, we did not observe any alteration in the expression of Synaptotagmin-7 (Syt-7) (Figure 4J), which is a PKA substrate and has been reported to contribute to the GLP-1R-induced GSIS (Wu et al., 2015).
evidence: Stated in the text with citation to published literature.

claim: Saturated fatty acid palmitate promotes fatty acid oxidation leading to enhanced generation of reactive oxidants that causes lipotoxicity.
source: The saturated fatty acid palmitate promotes fatty acid oxidation leading to the enhanced generation of reactive oxidants that causes lipotoxicity (Oprescu et al., 2007).
evidence: Stated in the text with citation to published literature.

claim: MS-275 prevented palmitate-induced death in MIN-6 cells and human islets.
source: These data in BRIN-BD11 pancreatic beta cells are in agreement with the observations reported in MIN-6 cells and human islets treated with MS-275 (Plaisance, 2014).
evidence: Stated in the text with citation to published literature.

claim: β-oxidative activity is associated with increased superoxide generation, oxidative stress, and apoptosis.
source: Since the β-oxidative activity was associated with increased superoxide generation (Rosca et al., 2012), oxidative stress, and apoptosis (Ye et al., 2019; Roma and Jonas, 2020), we compared the impact of palmitate on the expression of the genes involved in the pathway.
evidence: Stated in the text with citations to published literature.

claim: MS-275 has been reported to enhance oxidative metabolism and white adipose tissue (WAT) browning.
source: Previous reports described MS-275-mediated enhanced oxidative metabolism and white adipose tissue (WAT) browning (Galmozzi et al., 2013; Ferrari et al., 2017); however, the reports on the effect of GLP-1R signaling on energy expenditure were contradictory.
evidence: Stated in the text with citations to published literature.

claim: Reports on the effect of GLP-1R signaling on energy expenditure are contradictory.
source: Previous reports described MS-275-mediated enhanced oxidative metabolism and white adipose tissue (WAT) browning (Galmozzi et al., 2013; Ferrari et al., 2017); however, the reports on the effect of GLP-1R signaling on energy expenditure were contradictory.
evidence: Stated in the text as a summary of published literature.

claim: Some studies showed GLP-1 analogs contribute to fatty acid oxidation and WAT browning.
source: Although in some studies GLP-1 analogs have been shown to contribute to fatty acid oxidation and WAT browning (Kooijman et al., 2015), other studies in the animal model and humans reported no change or even a decrease in the energy expenditure upon incretin treatment (van Eyk et al., 2020; Horowitz et al., 2012).
evidence: Stated in the text with citations to published literature.

claim: Other studies reported no change or decrease in energy expenditure upon incretin treatment in animal models and humans.
source: Although in some studies GLP-1 analogs have been shown to contribute to fatty acid oxidation and WAT browning (Kooijman et al., 2015), other studies in the animal model and humans reported no change or even a decrease in the energy expenditure upon incretin treatment (van Eyk et al., 2020; Horowitz et al., 2012).
evidence: Stated in the text with citations to published literature.

claim: The SCALE Maintenance randomized clinical study showed similar weight gain after withdrawal of liraglutide during follow-up after 56-week treatment.
source: The data aligns with The SCALE Maintenance randomized clinical study where similar weight gain was noticed after the withdrawal of liraglutide during follow-up after 56-week treatment (Wadden et al., 2013).
evidence: Stated in the text with citation to published clinical study.

claim: MS-275 being a more selective HDAC inhibitor was better tolerated as monotherapy or when combined with other forms of cancer therapy in clinical trials.
source: In this regard, MS-275 being a more selective HDAC inhibitor was better tolerated as monotherapy or when combined with the other forms of cancer therapy in clinical trials for solid tumors and hematological malignancies (Connolly et al., 2017).
evidence: Stated in the discussion with citation to published literature.

claim: T2D is heterogeneous and polygenic with high familial risk.
source: The disease is heterogeneous and polygenic (Asalla et al., 2016), and with high familial risk (van Tilburg et al., 2001).
evidence: Stated in the discussion with citations to published literature.

claim: The pathophysiology of T2D represents a complex interaction of susceptible genes and environment through epigenetic modifications.
source: The pathophysiology thus represents a complex interaction of the susceptible genes and the environment through epigenetic modifications that influence its occurrence and progression (Raciti et al., 2015).
evidence: Stated in the discussion with citation to published literature.

claim: DNA methylation regulates Adcy-8 promoter activity in peripheral blood monocytes and high-grade cervical cancers.
source: DNA methylation but not acetylation is known to regulate the Adcy-8 promoter activity in peripheral blood monocytes (Gunawardhana et al., 2014), as well as in high-grade cervical cancers (Shen-Gunther et al., 2016).
evidence: Stated in the discussion with citations to published literature.

claim: Altered mitochondrial dynamics and enhanced fragmentation due to fatty acid stress have been linked to pancreatic beta-cell death.
source: Furthermore, altered mitochondrial dynamics and enhanced fragmentation due to fatty acid stress had been linked to pancreatic beta-cell death (Wiederkehr and Wollheim, 2009).
evidence: Stated in the discussion with citation to published literature.

claim: Hepatic IGF-1 has anti-inflammatory effects.
source: In the combined treatment group, we observed a 3.13 ± 0.15 fold increase of hepatic IGF-1 (p<0.01, one-way ANOVA, Tukey's multiple comparison test, Figure 9—figure supplement 2) in the liver tissue that was known to have the anti-inflammatory effect (Hribal et al., 2013).
evidence: Stated in the text with citation to published literature.
